text: In text RAG, the biggest failure usually happens before generation. The retriever simply does not bring the right evidence into the prompt.
When teams add PDFs, dashboards, product screenshots and training videos, a text only index misses many useful signals.
A practical multimodal RAG system converts each artifact into a searchable representation while preserving a pointer back to the original source.
For charts and diagrams, one common pattern is caption indexing. A vision model writes a concise factual summary, and that summary is embedded.
For video, the first version should usually be transcript based. Chunk the transcript by topic or time window and store start and end timestamps.
Calling a vision model for every image during every query is expensive. Retrieve candidate images cheaply, then use vision only on the top evidence.
Evaluation should ask whether the correct modality was retrieved, whether source citations were preserved, and whether visual evidence was interpreted accurately.
The user experience improves when answers say which part came from the PDF, which came from the chart, and which came from the video timestamp.
